title: Appropriateness of New Zealand's Smoke-free Generation Law for Singapore
what_it_is: Appropriateness of New Zealand's Smoke-free Generation Law for Singapore

sections.label: New Zealand smokefree generation law review
sections.summary: Asked whether the Ministry reviewed New Zealand's smokefree generation law and its appropriateness for Singapore; it will monitor international developments.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health whether the Ministry has reviewed the impact of New Zealand’s smokefree generation law and its potential appropriateness and effectiveness in Singapore’s context.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We will continue to monitor international developments and learn from the experiences of other countries in the area of tobacco control.

sections.label: Tobacco control measures and smoking prevalence
sections.summary: Policy measures, preventive education, cessation programmes and tax prohibitions have helped lower smoking prevalence to an all-time low of 8.4% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This includes having a comprehensive mix of policy measures, public preventive education, as well as cessation programmes, including also our tax prohibitions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: These efforts have helped us to see a decline in the smoking prevalence, and at this juncture we have achieved an all-time low of 8.4% in 2024.

sections.label: Tobacco-free generation implementation concerns
sections.summary: New Zealand and Malaysia repealed or removed such legislation, the UK announced plans, and Singapore remains open while engaging advocate Dr Koong Heng Nung.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As I mentioned, New Zealand has decided to repeal this legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Malaysia, also, who had announced it, had also removed it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Yes, UK had announced plans in October 2023 for a generation that will not be legally able to purchase tobacco in their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We have concerns about how the implementation will be carried out, and so we are mindful as to how this would affect the implementation here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We are continuing to be open to this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will announce if there are any movements in this front.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: You would be interested to know that we continue to be in engagement with Dr Koong Heng Nung, who was the original advocate of tobacco-free generation and we remain open to see how this can evolve.
